reason: The text contains named characters who are not leaders. Specifically, Ahiman (אחימן), Sheshai (שׁשי), and Talmai (תלמי) are named individuals described as 'yəlīdē hā'ānāq' (children of Anak) - inhabitants and giants of the land being scouted. These men are presented as obstacles or inhabitants of Canaan, not as leaders of the Israelite community. While the twelve spies are explicitly called 'ראשי בני־ישראל' (heads/leaders of the children of Israel), and figures like Moses, Aaron, Caleb, and Joshua function as leaders, Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai are named but are not leaders in any sense relevant to the narrative.
